links.outcome: Appropriate referral for coronary angiography, AI-augmented vs standard decision-making, in randomized trial
links.effect: AUROC 0.63 intervention vs 0.55 control; difference 0.09 (95% CI -0.22 to 0.39); did not meet non-inferiority margin of -0.05. Sensitivity 64.2% vs 55.1%; specificity 98.6% vs 99.2%.
links.quote: AI–augmented decision-making in stress echocardiography did not meet the non-inferiority end point when evaluated in a large, prospective randomized controlled trial, but may be beneficial in low-volume centers.

links.outcome: Clinician decision-making with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
links.effect: AI-augmented clinicians had AUROC 0.63 vs 0.55 for control, difference 0.09 (95% CI -0.22 to 0.39); non-inferiority not met; potential benefit in low-volume centers.
links.quote: The difference between the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for the intervention (0.63; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.43 to 0.83) and control (0.55; 95% CI, 0.33 to 0.80), did not meet the prespecified non-inferiority margin of −0.05 (difference, 0.09; 95% CI, −0.22 to 0. 39).

screen.reason: Prospective multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating the clinical efficacy of an AI-augmented decision support system versus standard clinician care in stress echocardiography referral.
